We were told by the nurse at the check in point that the wait time was at least 6 hrs before he would be seen by anyone and we were basically turned away and told to go home The next day when his fever hit over 104 we took him to the XXXXXXXXXXXXX unit Even though you could visibly see how sick he was it still was at least an hour before we got seen by a triage nurse. Once we did get seen the nurses and doctors were amazing and got him on medication quickly and had tests run on him My main complaint is with 1) the XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX being a unit with peds in it - being so unhelpful and and 2) how long it took someone to look at a baby We understand hospitals are busy, especially with COVID but we were very disappointed how long it took to get someone to look at someone so young

input: Hospital was at its full capacity, I slept in the hall way. It was very cold and loud to the point where I did not get any sleep. When I was admitted, I was not yet diagnosed but the doctors told me the worst case scenario possible without doing any further tests. At this point I was mentally/emotionally down. As each day went by, they ruled out what I did not have, but yet stated the illnesses I may have. I didn't like this process because it made me more sick - in a way very anxious/sad/etc. I did not know what I had. All the tests came out negative, I got a biopsy done then was discharged and sent home. It took more than 4 weeks to hear back from a doctor about my results. During this time I was out in the open just waiting helplessly. Overall, I did not like my hospital stay. Also when I requested a room the nurses told me I would be accommodated but never was.

input: Everyone treated me well. I was having hip surgery in the next couple of weeks and suddenly started having pain that was different, I thought it was in my abdomen, not my groin so felt it should be checked out. They did a CAT scan and decided it was muscular even though it felt like something was about to burst. The hardest part for me was waiting for the CAT scan as it was impossible for me to sit in a chair, I lay back in the recliner chair which I managed to do although I had a lot of discomfort. I was in that waiting room close to 2 hours. Others who came in after me were taken ahead of me, maybe they were in more pain, I don't know, but I was there a total of 5 hours. I'm not complaining, just stating a fact. I understand it's hard when people are hurting. In the end, I was told it was muscular and my surgeon's office put me in for surgery 2 weeks early. I appreciate everything that was done for me.

input: I feel like the nurses were amazing.  However, the doctor seemed to not be too concerned with listening to what was bothering me, she sent me for an ultrasound on areas surrounding the area I was having problems with and she seemed to be trying to catch me in a lie (that's how it felt anyway).  As a First Nations person, I rarely go to the hospital, I don't do drugs and would never go to the hospital just for pain meds.  I rarely accept pain meds when I am there.  This is the first time I've ever felt this way.  I ended up returning almost a week later for the same issue and had much better care from a second doctor who actually listened to me.  It's been almost two weeks and I'm still having pain and can't figure out what is causing it, but I doubt if I will return to the hospital to have it taken care of.

input: My only issue was the chest tube caused some nerve damage and I had difficulty controlling the pain the day before I left the hospital and for 2 weeks following surgery at home.  It is my understanding that nerve damage is common with this type of surgery.  I was told by the nurse that the damage was internal and that nothing could be done to help with the pain.  After 2 weeks at home and still having trouble with pain, I contacted my family doctor and he provided me with a prescription for Lyrica which finally gave me the relief I needed.  The discharge papers clearly say that I should contact a doctor with any issues so I accept full responsibility for waiting too long.  Assuming this is a common issue, my recommendation would be to educate any patient that may be experiencing nerve damage prior to leaving the hospital and to suggest contacting their doctor without delay to obtain the appropriate medication.

I wound up hiring a consultant to come to my home after I was discharged, and I credit this consultation with the success I have had breastfeeding my baby.

We came to the hospital through the emergency room and were notified immediately that we would be admitted to the oncology floor for at least a few days.
